title: The booking trigger, the schedule shape, the ALS booking reference and the plan-timer mechanism are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Legacy RWB-E3-010 sections 1 to 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 1865 to 1963); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.10; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T4 RESTRUCTURE and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41, 42 and 43; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 18; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-22 and R-RES-25; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03, DP-05, DP-10 and DP-13
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC2 to AC4; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.4; 12.5; 12.7; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the booking step. (1) TSD S2 T3.1 carries the schedule fields (booked_at, nleads_ref, first_due_date, installment_amount, installments, installments_paid, booking_difference) but defines no schedule entity, no booking record and no write operation for a booking, and the legacy story publishes no operation of its own. (2) No source states how the booking confirmation reaches rwb-treatment: the legacy build took an in-process callback, Architecture v5 slide 42 gives TreatmentBooked (EV-11) with rwb-payment as producer and rwb-treatment as one of two consumers, and the Temporal and Drools Design names BOOKING_MATCH, booking confirmed, as a Drools package without naming its trigger or its payload. (3) No source defines the payload, key or envelope of EV-11, although the stage needs the case identifier and both acknowledgement references to decide R-RES-22. (4) The plan timers are described as timers; no source states whether they are rows in the timer table, which is rwb-case's, or durable Temporal timers inside the stage workflow, and the catalogue retires TimerDue in favour of timers inside the workflow. (5) No source states the cadence of the plan clock, the end of the timer set, or how a due-date change moves a running timer. (6) The outbound interface of AC1 is named by no source: the FSD keeps booking in the core bank out of scope and the TSD records INT-03 and INT-26 as booked or submitted by the officer, while the only external cell Architecture v5 gives S2 is a Nexus operation into ACE Common.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-009, -012, -023, -028, -029, -031, -032, with no schedule or booking entity) and T-A.1 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004, none of them a booking); TSD S2 T5.1 (INT-03 'Booked by the officer; confirmed on the next day's load', INT-26 'Submitted by the officer in NLEADS', INT-34 'Published module interface'); FSD S2 v3 A1.1 ('Out of scope. ... booking in the core bank, which the officer does') and A2.10.2 ('Integration points. NLEADS, ALS and GL'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 event 11 ('TreatmentBooked | rwb-payment | rwb.payment.events.v1 | rwb-case, rwb-treatment') and event 18 ('TimerDue | durable timer | - | (retired: timer inside the workflow)'), slide 43 event 29 (case router as signal), slide 41 (rwb_treatment owners: treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers) and slide 13 (S2 row: Nexus to ACE Common, events with P8); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18 steps 5 and 6 ('R-RES-16/21/22 - EV-11', 'Payment plan timers - R-RES-25') and slide 9 note (BOOKING_MATCH, booking confirmed); Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-22 and R-RES-25; legacy RWB-E3-010 Endpoints (one row, GET /api/recovery/v1/treatments/{treatmentId})
area: Contract, event and clock: booking confirmation, schedule and plan timers
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-treatment with the P8 owner of the payment booking match and the platform workflow owner
proposed: Decide R-RES-22 on EV-11 rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1 consumed through this service's inbox, read the booking date and the schedule basis from v_ace_plan and v_ace_payment, write the seven schedule columns of TSD S2 T3.1 on treatment, and run the plan timers as durable timers inside TreatmentWorkflow with no timer row and no Schedule. Confirm the EV-11 payload and the timer cadence with the P8 owner and the platform workflow owner at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The booking and schedule element, its required set and the ALS acknowledgement reference are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Legacy RWB-E3-010 section 7 AC2 (record the booking date and set the payment schedule) and section 11 Data; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1 (treatment fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-RES-22 (ALS and NLEADS both acknowledge); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 event 11; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-03 and DP-13
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.7; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the booking body. (1) No source defines a booking element, an acknowledgement element or a schedule element, and the legacy story publishes no request or response shape for the booking step. (2) TSD S2 T3.1 marks the schedule columns as not required at column level, so no source fixes which facts a confirmation cannot be without. (3) R-RES-22 confirms a booking when ALS and NLEADS both acknowledge, but the TSD carries a NLEADS reference (nleads_ref) and no ALS reference at all, and no source states where the ALS reference is held. (4) No source states whether the booking difference is a required outcome, a free-form record or a text field, although DF-TRT-028 defines it as jsonb. (5) No source names the facts a plan clock starts from beyond first_due_date, nor whether the installment cadence is a parameter, a rule value or a reference row.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-023 nleads_ref only; DF-TRT-028 booking_difference jsonb; no ALS reference field) and T-A.1 (no booking operation); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-RES-22 ('WITH_OPS_BOOKING | BOOKING_CONFIRMED | ALS and NLEADS both acknowledge | Record the booking reference and set the payment schedule | BOOKED_IN_ALS_NLEADS'); legacy RWB-E3-010 section 7 AC2 ('Then record the booking date from v_ace_plan and set the payment schedule from v_ace_payment') and section 11 Data (v_ace_plan DF-ACE-160 to DF-ACE-177, treatment DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-014); FSD S2 v3 A2.10.3.1 (R-RES-22, R-RES-25, BR-S2-010); Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12
owner_role: Contract owner of rwb-treatment with the operations booking owner
proposed: Publish PlanBooking with eight properties: nleadsRef (DF-TRT-023), alsBookingRef (no column, carried on the booking record and the decision record), bookedAt (DF-TRT-012), firstDueDate (DF-TRT-029), installmentCount (DF-TRT-009), installmentAmount (DF-TRT-031), installmentsPaid (DF-TRT-032) and bookingDifference (DF-TRT-028). Make the first seven required because R-RES-22 needs both acknowledgements and R-RES-25 needs a first due date, and publish the required set with this gap so that no implementer invents a column for the ALS reference.

title: RWB-E3-010 AC1 sends the agreed terms to NLEADS and ALS from the Workbench, while the FSD and the TSD keep the booking with the officer in the core bank and in NLEADS
source: Legacy RWB-E3-010 section 7 AC1 and section 1 Story; FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A1.1 (out of scope: booking in the core bank, which the officer does); TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T5.1 (INT-03, INT-26); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (connection matrix, S2 row) and slide 42 event 11; Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence
section: 2 Business rationale; 7 Acceptance criteria (AC1 note); 8 Business rules; 12.2; 12.5; 19 Out of scope
description: A conflict of responsibility, and a gap behind it. Legacy AC1 and the legacy story text say the Workbench sends the agreed terms to NLEADS and ALS through the outbound interface, while the FSD puts booking in the core bank out of scope because the officer does it and the TSD records INT-03 as booked by the officer and INT-26 as submitted by the officer in NLEADS. Architecture v5 gives S2 no direct outbound cell to ALS, NLEADS or any outside system: its only external cell in the connection matrix is a Nexus operation into ACE Common, and the booking enters rwb-treatment again as EV-11 from rwb-payment. No source names that Nexus operation, its request or its answer, so the frame in which a Workbench-side booking instruction would travel is unspecified. Template and Rules R3 puts the Architecture v5 catalogue above the FSD, so the target cannot keep a Workbench outbound call to ALS and NLEADS as written.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E3-010 section 1 ('I want the Workbench to send the plan to NLEADS and ALS through the outbound interface') and AC1 ('Then it sends the agreed terms to NLEADS and ALS through the outbound interface'); FSD S2 v3 A1.1 ('Out of scope. ... booking in the core bank, which the officer does'); TSD S2 v2 T5.1 rows INT-03 ('Core bank (ALS) | Out | Booked by the officer; confirmed on the next day's load') and INT-26 ('NLEADS | Out | Submitted by the officer in NLEADS'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (row 'S2 Treatment': Nexus to ACE Common, events with P8, no outside cell) and slide 42 event 11; Template and Rules v1 R3 item 1 above item 7
area: Responsibility: booking in ALS and NLEADS
owner_role: Solution architect with the operations booking owner and the ACE Common owner
proposed: Keep the booking act with operations in ALS and NLEADS, as the FSD and the TSD state. rwb-treatment sends a booking instruction only through the one outbound path Architecture v5 gives it, a Temporal Nexus operation into the ACE Common namespace ace-collection, and confirms the booking from the v_ace_plan read and from EV-11; AC1 is proved end to end by the wave 2 integration harness. Confirm the Nexus operation name and its answer with the ACE Common owner at the wave 2 contract freeze.
